last_run.broken_assumption: Scaling HumanityAI mainly means adding more agents, tasks, evidence records, and review capacity inside one shared repository. At 100x-10,000x scale, the scarce resource becomes trustworthy integration across independently evolving domains, not raw agent throughput.
last_run.scale_scenario: Assume thousands of agents and human contributors work concurrently across many problem domains. A single global queue, shared state file, central evidence corpus, and maintainer review funnel would create contention, context overload, correlated mistakes, and authority concentration even if every individual contribution follows today's rules.

strongest_ideas.name: Federated evidence cells with narrow interface contracts
strongest_ideas.idea: Treat future HumanityAI as a federation of independently testable domain cells rather than one giant agent swarm. Each cell owns a bounded problem/evidence namespace and can evolve its internal workflow independently, but exports only a small signed/versioned public contract: claims, provenance, uncertainty, contradictions, forecasts, dependency references, and review status. A thin integration layer reasons across cells without gaining authority to silently rewrite their source records.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: The project currently coordinates work primarily through repository-wide schemas, tasks, PRs, and shared project state. This proposal makes interfaces rather than internal implementation the durable scaling unit, allowing independent teams or future repositories/services to interoperate without one central agent understanding everything.
strongest_ideas.evidence_analogy: NASA systems engineering treats interface definition, responsibility, change authority, compatibility, verification, and configuration control as first-class concerns when work is divided among parties. The transferable principle is to control the boundary while allowing internals to remain locally owned.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Reduces merge contention and cognitive load, contains domain-specific errors, permits heterogeneous methods, enables independent replication or replacement of a cell, and makes decentralization operational rather than rhetorical.
failure_modes: Poorly chosen boundaries can hide important cross-domain causal relationships.
Interface contracts can ossify too early and slow epistemic improvements.
Cells may develop incompatible confidence semantics or duplicate evidence.
A central integration layer could become a new authority bottleneck if it is allowed to adjudicate rather than expose disagreement.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Domain cells should not gain unilateral authority over affected populations merely because they own a namespace. Cross-cell integration must preserve minority/contradictory views and constitutional constraints.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High as a conceptual/read-only experiment; no repository split is required to test the contract idea.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Pick two existing problem domains and independently serialize each into a deliberately narrow interface object without changing source records. Ask a fresh integration agent to answer one cross-domain question using only those exported objects. Record what information was missing or ambiguous. Reject federation if the interface must expose nearly the entire internal corpus to remain useful.

strongest_ideas.name: Cross-cell challenge protocol instead of central truth arbitration
strongest_ideas.idea: At large scale, route disagreements between domain cells into explicit challenge objects rather than asking a central model to pick a winner. A challenge records the conflicting claims, shared definitions, decisive evidence sought, forecasts that would discriminate between views, and expiry/revisit conditions. Independent agents can then compete to resolve the uncertainty while both source positions remain intact.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: HumanityAI already preserves contradiction, but large-scale coordination will need a protocol for disagreements that cross ownership boundaries. This turns conflict itself into schedulable research without creating a central epistemic sovereign.
strongest_ideas.evidence_analogy: NASA interface-management guidance emphasizes explicit interface ownership, compatibility checks, controlled change, and capturing rationale/assumptions when multiple parties must integrate. HumanityAI can import the coordination structure while replacing engineering compatibility disputes with evidence-seeking challenges.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Makes cross-domain uncertainty actionable, supports parallel independent work, and limits pressure to erase disagreement merely to keep a unified knowledge graph tidy.
failure_modes: Challenge volume could explode faster than useful resolution capacity.
Agents may manufacture superficial disagreements to create tasks.
Some normative conflicts cannot be resolved by additional evidence.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Normative/value disputes must be labeled rather than disguised as empirical challenges; constitutional or consequential governance conflicts remain human-governed.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High; challenge objects can begin as an optional derived layer.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Find one real contradiction spanning two current evidence/problem areas and write a temporary challenge object specifying what observation or source would materially update each side. If no useful discriminating test can be expressed, document whether the disagreement is definitional, normative, or structurally cross-domain.

rejected_or_deferred: Immediately split HumanityAI into many repositories: organizational partition before testing interface boundaries would create fragmentation and operational overhead.
Use one increasingly powerful coordinator model over every domain: this scales context and authority together and creates a correlated failure point.
Let every cell invent arbitrary schemas: local autonomy without stable interfaces would make integration and independent verification progressively harder.

evidence_checked.title: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook — Interface Management
evidence_checked.supports: When development is divided among parties, interfaces should be explicitly defined, owned, controlled, checked for compatibility, verified, and updated through controlled change.

evidence_checked.title: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook — Interface Requirements Document Outline
evidence_checked.supports: Interface documents should state purpose/scope, precedence, responsibility and change authority, then define the interface rather than duplicate higher-level documents.

last_run.recommended_next_test: Prototype federation only as a read-only interface exercise across two existing domains. Measure information loss, ambiguity, cross-domain usefulness, and whether independent ownership actually reduces coupling before changing architecture.

notes: Frontier state records conceptual experiments, not authority. Ideas may exceed current execution permissions; human-review boundaries remain governed by security/policy.json.
